stories.title: Ranked 92nd In The World: Nigeria’s 45 Destinations Without A Prior Visa And The Burden Of Restricted Mobility, By Daniel Nduka Okonkwo
stories.description: This is best understood by those who have travelled. Restricted mobility is a difficulty Nigerians face repeatedly, and it is often the first hurdle between a capable Nigerian and an opportunity abroad. The record shows how costly that hurdle can be. Access is narrow and unstable: Henley placed Nigeria 89th, with 44 destinations in April; 90th, with 44 in July; and 92nd, with 45 in October. Its April report also records that Nigeria lost visa-free entry to several destinations in recent years, including Zambia, Zimbabwe, and Lesotho.

From robots, drones and electric vehicles to towering skyscrapers and global tech giants, Shenzhen represents Beijing’s vision of a modern superpower. But behind the spectacular skyline lies a more complicated reality. stories.title: Assessing the carbon emissions and energy consumption of US hyperscale data centres
stories.description: The rapid proliferation of hyperscale data centres (HDCs) in the USA—mainly driven by the adoption of artificial intelligence—has raised concerns about this industry’s carbon footprint. We compiled facility-level information on 403 US hyperscale data centres operating between May 2024 and April 2025 and estimated their electricity consumption, electricity sources and attributable CO2 emissions. Across facility-load scenarios, these HDCs consumed approximately 68–99 TWh of electricity and were associated with approximately 21–31 million metric tons of CO2 under a location-based, total-output balancing-authority attribution method. Under the central scenario, HDC electricity demand was approximately 82 TWh, corresponding to about 1.8% of total US electricity consumption, and attributable CO2 emissions were approximately 25.7 Mt. Roughly 54% of attributed generation was supplied by fossil-fuel sources. The HDC electricity-weighted total-output carbon intensity was approximately 314 gCO2 kWh−1, compared with a US total-output average of approximately 348 gCO2 kWh−1. Our approach provides a facility-resolved attributional framework for assessing the carbon footprint of hyperscale data centres using plant-level electricity-generation and emissions data. The growing number of hyperscale data centres raises concerns about their environmental impacts. This study presents a facility-resolved attributional framework to assess the carbon footprint of hyperscale data centres in the USA using plant-level electricity-generation and emissions data.

stories.title: Mapping the Tibetan Plateau microbiome across ecosystems provides a resource for biodiscovery
stories.description: Microbial genetics can inspire innovations in biotechnology, but many microbial communities remain poorly understood. The genetic repertoire of high-mountain microbiomes remains largely untapped for biotechnology. Here we present the Tibetan Environmental Genome (TEG) catalogue, comprising 51,921 metagenome-assembled genomes from 1,698 environmental samples spanning 868 sites across 6 terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems of the Tibetan Plateau, Earth’s highest and largest mountain region. The TEG spans 105 phyla encompassing 17,920 species, of which nearly 90% are previously uncharacterized. Importantly, TEG establishes a comprehensive repository for biodiscovery, revealing 44,719 biosynthetic gene clusters, 19,168 candidate antimicrobial peptides, 1,262 low-identity CRISPR–Cas systems and 1,077 candidate polyethylene terephthalate hydrolases. To validate these findings, 29 candidate antimicrobial peptides were synthesized and all exhibited inhibitory activity against at least 1 of 7 tested pathogens, with 5 showing broad-spectrum activity. This catalogue reveals a rich and previously inaccessible pool of enzymes, bioactive compounds and programmable molecular systems, establishing a foundational resource for discovery and application in biotechnology. The Tibetan Environmental Genome catalogue is composed of over 50,000 metagenome-assembled genomes sourced from terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems across the Tibetan Plateau.

The team says these new details provide clues about the early formation of the Beta Pictoris system and collisions that may still be occurring.
